selection.method: Source-only selection from public AWS, Strands, and independent repositories after Amazon P0 implementation in #350. No HorusTrace output from this cohort was used to select cases. Every target is pinned to an exact commit SHA and scanned at an application-level path where practical.
selection.interpretation: Amazon expansion validation holdout. Cases exercise current Strands Python/TypeScript, managed Bedrock Agent declarations in CloudFormation/Terraform, current AgentCore project configuration, AgentCore Terraform, hybrid Bedrock/Strands/MCP layouts, and AWS execution-role authority reconstruction.

cases.source_signal: Repository-structured Strands research agent combines Agent, MCPClient, session management and multiple local tool modules; stresses cross-file tool/MCP binding and conservative destination reconstruction.

Strands audit agent uses BedrockModel, custom tools, high-authority vended tools including shell/http/editor/python and an agent-as-tool/document-agent pattern; validates effect projection and delegation.
Compact Strands application combines Agent, stdio MCPClient and file_write in an A2A integration; validates local MCP transport and write authority without monorepo contamination.
TypeScript Strands Agent deployed for AgentCore imports Agent, tool and BedrockModel from @strands-agents/sdk; validates the separate TypeScript adapter on real source.
CloudFormation application declares AWS::Bedrock::Agent and related execution infrastructure; validates managed-agent discovery and source-visible role/action-group authority.

Modular Terraform Bedrock Agent references an execution role whose inline policy is defined through aws_iam_role_policy plus data.aws_iam_policy_document; directly tests repository-level IAM authority correlation.

Terraform creates one supervisor and a for_each set of child Bedrock Agents, then routes among them through Step Functions/Lambda. Expected inventory is multi-agent; delegation may remain partially resolved if orchestration cannot be statically joined.

Real solution binds a managed Bedrock Agent action group to a Lambda-hosted Strands MCP client and knowledge-base/IAM infrastructure; validates action-group ownership and cross-stack hybrid authority.
Current AgentCore v1 project config declares a PUBLIC HTTP container runtime with explicit entrypoint/codeLocation. Validates post-migration agentcore/agentcore.json runtime discovery.
Current AgentCore config includes runtime/memory plus DataAnalystToolsGateway with PostgreSQL Lambda-backed tools; validates gateway/target authority in a non-trivial first-party project.
Independent integration uses current AgentCore CodeZip runtime, PUBLIC HTTP, requestHeaderAllowlist and session storage. Tests current config generalization outside AWS sample repositories.
Independent current AgentCore project declares a CodeZip PYTHON_3_13 runtime using protocol MCP and PUBLIC networking for a stateful FastMCP meeting scheduler.
Current Terraform AgentCore MCP runtime binds aws_bedrockagentcore_agent_runtime to an execution role and Cognito CUSTOM_JWT authorizer; validates runtime identity and authentication evidence.

Independent Terraform uses aws_bedrockagentcore_runtime for a support agent rather than the newer provider spelling seen in first-party samples; deliberately tests resource-name/schema drift and conservative unresolved handling.
